# Parity Across Languages

How to keep one tool implemented in several languages, such as the skill library helper's
PowerShell, Bash and Python variants, behaviourally identical.

## Contract

- One specification of commands, arguments, messages, exit codes and persisted state applies to
  every variant. Accept the same flag spellings in each (the helper accepts `-Version` and
  `-Related` in Bash and Python too), and print the same messages and table columns.
- Keep any state file format identical, so a workspace can switch variant between runs.
- Document every variant's runtime prerequisites; the variant that needs the most should check them
  first and fail with a message naming the missing tool.

## Shared Fixtures

- Commit input fixtures, such as a catalog, once in a `fixtures/` folder that every suite reads.
  When a fixture is generated by tooling in one language, add a test that regenerates it and
  compares, so the committed copy cannot drift.
- Share one fake for each external command where the suites can run it. A Bash fake serves pytest
  and bats on Linux; PowerShell suites on Windows keep their own fake with the same behaviour.
- Keep fixtures and fakes LF-only, and track executable fakes as mode `100755`.

## Scenario Lists

- Give each behaviour the same test name in every suite, in the same order, so a missing scenario
  is visible by comparing titles.
- Write assertions that hold for every variant: compare whole messages, and match tables with
  whitespace-tolerant patterns rather than exact column padding.
- A scenario only one language can express, such as a fixture-drift check, lives in that suite and
  says so in its name.

## Changes

- Change every variant, and every suite, in one commit. A pull request that changes one variant
  without the others fails review, even when CI is green.
- Run all suites before committing: natively where the toolchain exists, otherwise in the
  containers the [pytest](pytest.md) and [bats](bats.md) references name.
